questions.q: How many people must be in a room before there is a greater than 50% chance that at least one of them shares your exact birthday (not just any two people sharing a birthday with each other)?

Three prisoners each have a hat that is independently red or blue with 50% probability. Each can see the other two hats but not their own, and all three must simultaneously guess their own hat colour or pass. They win only if at least one guesses and everyone who guesses is correct. Using the optimal strategy — guess the opposite colour of what you see if the other two hats match, otherwise pass — what is their probability of winning?
Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. You're told at least one of them shows a 6. What is the probability that the other die also shows a 6?

100 prisoners, each assigned a unique number 1-100, must each find their own number among 100 boxes by opening at most 50 boxes (the room is reset between prisoners; no communication once it starts). If every prisoner follows the strategy 'open the box matching my number, then open the box matching the number found inside, and repeat,' what is the approximate probability that all 100 prisoners succeed?
